theme.title: Heat wave
theme.subtitle: Miami Heat, 2012–13
theme.recap: Miami won 27 in a row on the way to a second straight title, five years after a 15-win season.

questions.prompt: How long was the Miami Heat's 2012–13 winning streak?

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: the Heat embarked on a 27-game winning streak

funFacts.text: The winning run began with a Super Bowl Sunday victory over Toronto and eventually became a franchise record.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: The Heat defeated the Toronto Raptors on Super Bowl Sunday to start what would become the longest winning streak

funFacts.text: Miami rallied from a huge third-quarter deficit in Cleveland during the run, then won the game.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: The Heat overcame a league high 27-point third-quarter deficit to defeat the Cleveland Cavaliers

funFacts.text: Chicago finally stopped Miami's historic run in late March, although the Heat would still secure the top East seed.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: The Heat fall 101–97 to the Chicago Bulls, ending their winning streak

questions.prompt: How many three-pointers did Shane Battier make in Game 7 of the 2013 Finals?
questions.context: 2013 NBA Finals · Game 7 · vs San Antonio

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Battier scored 18 points on six 3-pointers

funFacts.text: With the series in the balance, Battier defended Tim Duncan's missed close-range shot and follow-up attempt.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Duncan, guarded by Shane Battier, missed a shot under the basket and a follow-up tip-in attempt

funFacts.text: The championship decider followed Ray Allen's unforgettable game-tying three-pointer in the preceding matchup.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Ray Allen made a game-tying three-pointer to send Game 6 to overtime

funFacts.text: Battier's bench scoring offset scoreless performances from Chris Bosh and Ray Allen in the deciding game.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Battier scored 18 points on six 3-pointers to offset scoreless nights by Bosh and Allen

questions.prompt: In 2012–13 Miami became the first team to win how many games in a single calendar month?

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: becoming the first team in NBA history to win at least 17 games in a calendar month

funFacts.text: During that remarkable stretch, Miami completed a sweep of all opposing NBA franchises by beating Indiana.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: the Heat beat every single team in the NBA with their victory against the Indiana Pacers

funFacts.text: Miami even won in San Antonio while James, Wade and Chalmers were out of the lineup.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: The Heat defeated the San Antonio Spurs 88-86 without all-stars LeBron James and Dwyane Wade

funFacts.text: Comebacks became routine: Miami erased a double-digit deficit against Detroit late in the streak.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: The Heat overcame an 11-point deficit to defeat the Detroit Pistons

questions.prompt: Chris "Birdman" Andersen shot what percentage from the field in the 2013 playoffs?

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Chris "Birdman" Andersen shot 80.7 percent (46-of-57) from the field in the 2013 postseason

funFacts.text: Birdman arrived on a short ten-day contract in January rather than starting the year on Miami's roster.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: January 20: Chris Andersen signed to a ten-day contract

funFacts.text: Birdman's nickname came from his wingspan and shot-blocking style, not from his colorful tattoos.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Nicknamed "Birdman" for his wingspan and blocking prowess

funFacts.text: In the Finals against San Antonio, Andersen contributed off the bench rather than starting a game.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Chris Andersen  | 5  | 0  | 14.2
